column6: built in Storyspace ... in 1990: the work was written earlier (presented 1987) and published on disk in 1990; reworded to "published on disk in 1990"
older text (not changed): Explainer attributes the term "lexical paths" to Joyce; unverified. Old misconceptions bullets lack the (correction) format
stitching bullet: correction dropped the qualifier that models can reproduce memorized training text verbatim; added it
older text (not changed): Explainer and Q0 say the model picks "the most likely next token" (sampling is common); calls training "unsupervised" (self-supervised)
older text (not changed): Q3 explanation "Before calligrammes, poetry worked through language" conflicts with the new Herbert "Easter Wings" bullet

older text (not changed): Explainer calls Johnson "pivotal figure in modernist literature" (banned word; he is postwar); "form must be an extension of content" echoes Olson/Creeley, attribution to Johnson as his phrase is doubtful
older text (not changed): Core Idea "pioneered" and q4 explanation "would have lacked precedent" overstate (Mallarme, Apollinaire came earlier)
video bullet: "captures ... none of the interaction" overstated (a playthrough shows the player's interactions); reworded to say the viewer cannot make choices
older text (not changed): Core Idea and Q2 put kinetic poetry and constrained texts inside Aarseth's category without qualification; non-interactive kinetic poems are not ergodic by his definition
older text (not changed): Explainer etymology "from physics (ergo = work, ode = path)"; Aarseth gives Greek ergon + hodos
legal bullet: "Transformation is one factor" is imprecise; transformativeness is weighed within the first of four fair-use factors; reworded
older text (not changed): Q3 true-false "co-authorship in a way that traditional poetry never does" (answer true) conflicts with the new bullet on pre-computer chance and combinatorial procedures
older text (not changed): Core Idea says hypertext theory "developed the lexia concept"; the term is Barthes's (S/Z), adopted by Landow
Storyspace bullet dropped co-developer John B. Smith; added
older text (not changed): Core Idea credits lexia/multilinearity to Bolter and Joyce (Landow, after Barthes); q4 explanation cites Aarseth's "ergodic" terms as hypertext theory
older text (not changed, clearly wrong): Explainer twice places Little Sparta "in the Scottish Highlands"; it is in the Pentland Hills near Dunsyre, South Lanarkshire
